title.narrative: Women’s Economic Empowerment in the Cotton Value Chain
Women’s Economic Empowerment in the Cotton Value Chain

description.narrative:
The projects overall goal is Poverty, injustice and inequality in the cotton sector is reduced in Malawi, Mozambique, Zambia and Zimbabwe
The project has added one objective in addition to the four objectives in the previous phase:
Objective 1: Increased availability of, accessibility to and utilisation of productive resources, financial services and extension services among women and youth in the cotton value chain.
Objective 2: Women and female youth fully participate in processes in the cotton sub-sector and complimentary sectors at local and national levels that enhance sustainable livelihoods,business development and entrepreneurship.
Objective 3: Reduced vulnerability and increased resilience to negative environmental and climatic changes impacting smallholder cotton farmers.
Objective 4: Enhanced capacity of partner organisations to develop into strong, sustainable, rights-based, democratic, inclusive, transformative and adaptive entities and increasingly provide members with demand driven products and services to advocate for change to better outcomes for smallholder farmers in the cotton sector.
Objective 5: Strengthened capacity of cotton farmers and partner organisations to mobilise and organise around an advocacy agenda to influence key decision makers to adopt or amend policies to protect and affirm the rights of cotton farmers at regional level.

We Effect har samarbetat med Sida under den tidigare strategiperioden och har till Sida gett in ett 2-årigt projektförslag för strategiperioden 2022–2026. Projektet har för avsikt att bidra till att kvinnor och ungdomar ska få ekonomisk egenmakt i värdekedjan för bomullsproduktion. De viktigaste resultaten i fas 1 av insatsen var införandet av bomullscertifieringsstandarder och framtagandet av praxis för utvalda partnerorganisationer (PO), rensningsföretag och småbruksodlare av bomull i fokusländerna. Tonvikten lades också på att stärka producentorganisationernas kapacitet och involvera rensningsföretag i jämställdhet mellan könen, finansiell integration och tillhandahållande av utökad tjänsteleverans b.la. i form av kapacitetsstärkande åtgärder. Denna fas kommer att vara en fortsättning på den tidigare insatsen med ett starkt fokus på att kvinnor och ungdomar på landsbygden i bomullsvärdekedjan ska få ekonomisk egenmakt. Den betonar också diversifiering av inkomstkällor genom att uppmuntra målgrupperna att engagera sig i även inkomstkällor utanför bomull- och jordbrukssfären. Projektet har stora strategiska resultatområden, inklusive: Kvinnor och unga småbrukare av bomull och entreprenörer har anständiga arbetsvillkor, kvinnor och ungdomar som småbruksodlare har förbättrat avkastningen, kvinnor och unga småbrukare av bomull och entreprenörer har ökat sin disponibla inkomst och köpkraft. Projektet kommer att genomföras i fyra We Effect-fokusländer, Malawi, Moçambique, Zambia och Zimbabwe och projektets huvudmål är att ekonomiskt stärka kvinnor och ungdomar på landsbygden i bomullsvärdekedjan. Detta kommer att översättas till följande fyra specifika mål: - - Att öka tillgängligheten till och utnyttjandet av produktiva resurser, finansiella tjänster och utökad tjänsteleverans b.la. i form av kapacitetsstärkande åtgärder bland kvinnor och ungdomar i bomullsvärdekedjan. - Att få kvinnor och kvinnliga ungdomar att delta fullt ut i och på ett meningsfullt sätt påverka beslutsprocesser inom bomullsundersektorn på lokal, nationell och regional nivå. - Att minska sårbarheten och öka beroendet av negativa miljö- och klimatförändringar som påverkar småbruksodlare av bomull. - Att stärka partnerorganisationernas förmåga att påverka bomullspolitiken och företagsmiljön till förmån för småbrukare inom bomullssektorn. Den planerade budgeten är 18MSEK för 2 år från och med december 2022 och projektet riktar sig till 35 000 småbrukare, samt ytterligare 7 000 stödmottagare från föregående fas.

We Effect has been partnering with Sida in the previous strategy period and has submitted a 2-year project proposal under the strategy period 2022-2026. It intends to work towards women and youth economic empowerment in the cotton value chain.The main achievements in phase 1 intervention were introducing cotton certification standards and arranging practices to targeted partner organizations(POs), ginning companies, and smallholder cotton farmers in the focus countries.There was also emphasis on strengthening the capacity of the POs and involving ginning companies in gender equality, financial inclusion, and extension service delivery. This phase will be a continuation of the previous intervention with a strong focus on women and youth in rural areas in the cotton values chain to be economically empowered. It also emphasises on diversifying their income source by encouraging them to get into non cotton and non-farming engagements. The project has major strategic outcome areas including, Women and youth smallholder cotton farmers and entrepreneurs have decent jobs. Women and youth, the smallholder cotton farmers have improved yield Women and youth smallholder cotton farmers and entrepreneurs have increased disposable income and spending powerThe project will be implemented in four We Effect focus countries, Malawi, Mozambique, Zambia and Zimbabwe and the main objective of the project is to economically empower women and youth in the rural areas in cotton the value chain. This will be a translated into the following four specific objectives:- To Increase availability, accessibility to and utilisation of productive resources, financial and extension services among women and youth in the cotton value chain- To make women and female youth fully participate in and are able to meaningfully influence decision making processes in the cotton sub-sector at local, national and regional levels- To reduce vulnerability and increased reliance to negative environmental and climatic changes impacting on smallholder cotton farmers.- To strengthen the capacity of Partner Organisations to influence cotton policy and the business environment in favour of smallholder farmers in the cotton sector.The planned budget is 18MSEK for 2 years starting from December 2022 and the project targets 35,000 smallholder farmers, additional 7000 beneficiaries from the previous phase.

title.narrative: Amendment to the agreement We effect no 2

description.narrative:
The Womens Economic Empowerment in the Cotton Value Chain (WEECVC) project achieved significant progress in 2025 across Malawi, Mozambique, Zambia, and Zimbabwe, strengthening womens and youths economic, social, and environmental resilience. The project reached 36,548 rightsholders (102% of target), with women representing 61% of participants.
Economic Empowerment
Women and youth recorded measurable gains in income, diversification, and entrepreneurship. In Malawi, women engaged in diversification rose from 72.5% to 77.5% and non-agricultural enterprise income increased by 24%. Mozambique trained 1,271 women farmers in entrepreneurship, enabling diversification into sesame and small businesses. Study circles evolved into business platforms, with Zambia formalizing 19 groups into cooperatives.
Social Capital and Inclusion
Study circles and VSLAs strengthened collective action, leadership, and confidence. Membership reached 20,866, serving as the backbone for learning, financial inclusion, and enterprise development. Women increasingly participated in leadership and advocacy, with Malawi reporting women farmers with improved advocacy skills increased from 2,083 to 3,985.
Environmental Resilience
Climate smart agriculture adoption expanded. Malawi increased agroforestry practitioners from 3,703 to 3,888, while Zambia established over 1,000 agroforestry seedlings despite climate stress. Zimbabwe strengthened Integrated Pest Management (IPM), soil health, and safe pesticide use.
Financial Inclusion
VSLAs became a major driver of empowerment, with over 21,000 members accessing savings and loans. Mozambique achieved near universal financial inclusion, with 1,271 of 1,275 women accessing financial services. Zambia mobilized over K1.8 million in VSLA share outs.
Market Participation and Value Addition
Women increasingly engaged in value addition and structured markets. Malawi saw cotton value addition participation rise from 6% in 2024 to 28% in 2025. Zimbabwe and Zambia expanded weaving and processing activities, while digital market information improved access to buyers.
Unexpected Results
Key Unexpected Results
1. Transformative Ripple Effects of Womens Economic Empowerment. Womens increased income has generated impacts beyond household food security. Earnings are being reinvested in children's education, contributing to lower school dropout rates, particularly among girls. Improvements have been observed in family nutrition, child health, housing conditions, sanitation, and access to clean water, leading to healthier and more resilient communities.
2. New Market and Trade Linkages: Women entrepreneurs have proactively diversified into additional value chains such as sunflower, horticulture, livestock, sesame, cowpeas, and soybeans. Increased production has stimulated demand for value addition, processing, and higher quality standards. Market saturation in domestic markets has encouraged women to explore regional trade opportunities across neighboring countries.
3. Growing Regional Interest in ESACO Although ESACO was originally focused on Southern and Eastern Africa, countries from West Africa have expressed strong interest in joining the initiative. Ethiopia has already joined, demonstrating the initiatives. This expansion could promote stronger pan-African cooperation through integrated value chains, trade corridors, and policy harmonization.
4. Demand for a Broader Commodity Focus ESACO was initially established as a cotton-focused organization. Stakeholders and partner countries are increasingly requesting the inclusion of other commodities, including oilseeds, livestock, horticulture, and sesame. This has led to calls for ESACO to evolve from a cotton-focused platform into a broader commodity-based organization supporting multiple agricultural value chains across the region.
Overall Outcome
The initiative has delivered benefits far beyond its original goals by driving social development, stimulating entrepreneurship and market diversification, attracting wider regional participation, and creating demand for a broader agricultural value-chain approach across Africa.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
